content:
q28.

**Runners the server actually starts** (both wired in `server/server.go`, via `Server.startBackgroundRunners`, called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`):

- **s3presign runner** (`server/runner/s3presign`) — trigger: a plain `time.Ticker` firing every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27,30`), started as a goroutine from `server/server.go:162-171`. It also runs once immediately on startup via `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` (`server/server.go:163`) before the ticker loop begins.

That is the only background loop actually started by the server. Everything else in `startBackgroundRunners` is just bookkeeping (context/cancel tracking) for this one runner.

**Not a standalone runner, just an inline call:** `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`) is invoked directly and synchronously from request handlers in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447` (on memo create/update) — not scheduled at all, driven by the API request itself. The batch-processing `Runner`/`RunOnce` type in that same package (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:14-72`, meant to rebuild payloads for *all* memos in batches) has no caller anywhere — `NewRunner` for `memopayload` is never invoked outside its own file (confirmed via reference search), so this runner exists in the codebase but the server never starts it.

**Unused scheduling infrastructure:** `internal/scheduler` (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`) is a full GitHub-Actions-style cron scheduler supporting standard cron expressions (per its own `README.md` and `doc.go`). It is referenced only from its own test files (`example_test.go`, `integration_test.go`) — no production code (`cmd/memos/main.go`, `server/server.go`, or any router/service) imports `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler`. This is scheduling infrastructure present in the repo but not used by the running server; the one real scheduled job (s3presign) uses a hand-rolled `time.Ticker` instead of this cron package.
